message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the same ancestor that gave rise to all placental mammals.  
- **Taxonomic level:** The common ancestor lies at the base of the clade that contains the orders Carnivora (lions) and Perissodactyla (zebras).  
- **Time frame:** This ancestor lived roughly 100–120 million years ago, during the early Cretaceous period, before the diversification of the major placental mammal lineages.  

So, the lion and zebra share a common ancestor that is essentially the last common ancestor of all placental mammals.
